scams.title: UPI fraud
scams.how: You get a 'collect request', QR code or link and are told to scan it or enter your PIN to 'receive' money, often while selling something online.
flags: You must enter your UPI PIN to receive money
Buyer 'accidentally' sent extra money and wants a refund
do: Remember: a UPI PIN is only for sending money, never for receiving
Verify payments in your bank app, not via screenshots

scams.title: OTP / KYC scams
scams.how: Callers pretend to be from your bank, telecom provider or a delivery company and say your account or SIM will be blocked unless you share an OTP or update 'KYC'.
flags: Asking for OTP, PIN, CVV or card number
Requests to install screen-sharing apps (AnyDesk, TeamViewer)
do: Hang up and call the official number on your card or the bank's website
Do KYC only at the branch or official app

scams.title: Phishing
scams.how: Fake emails, SMS or WhatsApp messages with links to look-alike websites that steal your passwords or card details, or files that install malware.
flags: Urgent tone or 'you won a prize'
do: Type the website address yourself instead of clicking
Never install APK files sent on WhatsApp
Turn on 2FA so a stolen password isn't enough

scams.title: Fake job offers
scams.how: 'Work from home', 'like YouTube videos and earn', or overseas job offers that ask for a registration fee, deposit, or 'task investment' before paying you.
flags: Any fee to get a job
Telegram 'task' groups with small early payouts
Offer without a real interview or company email
do: Real employers don't charge you to hire you
Verify the company on its official website and LinkedIn
Check overseas recruiters are registered with the MEA's eMigrate portal

scams.title: Sextortion
scams.how: A stranger starts a video call or chat, records or fakes compromising images, then threatens to share them with your contacts unless you pay.
flags: Unknown video calls, especially at night
Rapid move from friendly chat to intimate requests
do: Don't pay: payment usually leads to more demands
Stop contact, save evidence (screenshots, profile links), and report the account
Report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930. You are the victim. It's not your fault

scams.title: 'Digital arrest' calls
scams.how: Fraudsters pose as police, CBI, customs or courier officials on a video call, claim you're linked to a crime, and demand money to 'clear your name'.
flags: Told not to tell family or disconnect
do: Indian law has no such thing as a 'digital arrest' over video call

habits: Use unique passwords with a password manager
Turn on two-factor authentication for email, banking and social media
Keep phone, apps and laptop updated
Install apps only from official app stores
Lock your SIM with a PIN and your phone with a strong screen lock
Back up important photos and documents
Review app permissions: does a torch app need your contacts?
Be careful about what you post publicly: location, ID cards, tickets

quiz.msg: Your electricity connection will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 PM because last month's bill was not updated. Call officer 98XXXXXX12 immediately.
quiz.why: Classic electricity-bill scam: urgency plus a personal mobile number. Power companies don't disconnect you via SMS from a 10-digit number. Check in your official DISCOM app.

quiz.msg: Dear customer, your KYC is pending. Your bank account will be blocked in 24 hours. Update now: sbi-kyc-update.top/verify
quiz.why: Fake KYC link on a lookalike domain. Banks never ask you to update KYC through an SMS link. Go to the branch or the official app.

quiz.msg: 123456 is your OTP to log in. Do not share it with anyone. It is valid for 5 minutes.
quiz.why: This is a normal OTP message, if YOU just tried to log in. It becomes a scam the moment someone calls asking you to read it out.

quiz.msg: This is CBI. A parcel in your name contains illegal items. Stay on this video call, you are under digital arrest. Transfer money for verification.
quiz.why: 'Digital arrest' doesn't exist. No police or agency arrests you on a video call or asks for money to 'verify' you. Hang up and call 1930.

quiz.msg: Congratulations! You won ₹25,00,000 in the KBC lottery. Pay a ₹5,000 processing fee to claim your prize.
quiz.why: You can't win a lottery you never entered, and real prizes don't need an upfront fee.

quiz.msg: Hi, your order has been shipped. Track it in the app you ordered from.
quiz.why: No link, no payment, no urgency, and it sends you to the official app. Still, open the app yourself rather than tapping any link.
